cards.explanation: The answer is False. The LORD was not pleased with the fathers. He says, "The LORD was very angry with your fathers." (Zechariah 1:2) That's the first thing Zechariah, the prophet, hears in this message. No warm-up, no small talk, just the plain truth up front, friends.

The answer is that they return to Him and He returns to them. Listen to how it's built, friends. "Return to Me, declares the LORD of Hosts, and I will return to you…" (Zechariah 1:3) The people take the first step, and the LORD promises to meet them. I think that's about the warmest door anybody ever held open.

The answer is that they did not listen. The LORD says of the fathers, "…they did not listen or pay attention to Me…" (Zechariah 1:4) The former prophets were the earlier messengers He sent them. The message was to turn from their evil ways and deeds, and the fathers didn't.

The answer is His words and statutes. God asks, "But did not My words and My statutes, which I commanded My servants the prophets, overtake your fathers?" (Zechariah 1:6) The prophets carried the message, but the words came from Him. And those words overtook the fathers. I think that's worth sitting with for a minute, friends.

The answer is True. After His words overtook them, the fathers "…repented and said…" (Zechariah 1:6) That means they finally turned around. The message they brushed off earlier caught up with them, and they came to see it, friends.

The word is "purposed." The fathers said, "Just as the LORD of Hosts purposed to do to us according to our ways and deeds, so He has done to us." (Zechariah 1:6) They looked back and said He had done what He purposed. That's a humble thing to say out loud, friends.
